key_concepts: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
Isotopes have the same number of protons but different mass numbers
Atomic number is determined by the number of protons and remains constant across isotopes
Mass number is the sum of protons and neutrons and varies among isotopes
Carbon-12 and Carbon-14 are isotopes of carbon
Hydrogen has isotopes called protium, deuterium, and tritium
Atomic mass is the weighted average mass of an element's isotopes
Relative abundance is the fraction or percentage of each isotope found in nature
Atomic mass is calculated using the formula: sum of isotope mass multiplied by relative ab
The calculated average atomic mass of chlorine from Cl-35 and Cl-37 is about 35.5 amu
Isotopes are used in carbon dating to determine the age of archaeological artifacts
Radioactive isotopes such as technetium-99 are used in medical imaging like PET scans
